name: crew
description: Makes the main session a lead that delegates to five specialist subagents: code-reader and research on Haiku; designer and developer on Sonnet; architect on Opus. The developer runs and reports its tests; the architect independently audits acceptance. With the jevKey option set (a TypeSafe key), Jev sizes only each call's effort, bounded to medium or high; models stay at role defaults or fixed twin ids, and any Jev request or config failure requests medium unless the agent has already sent its first step; that sends a redacted, truncated prompt to api.typesafe.ai. When a local HTTP loopback proxy is ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, each role also gets a fixed-model crew:<role>-codex twin. Calls may be routed automatically to those twins when Codex has more weekly headroom, with or without Jev; what those subagents read and write goes to OpenAI through the proxy.

jevKey.title: Jev API key (TypeSafe)
jevKey.description: Setting this key turns Jev routing on; leaving it empty turns it off. With a key, Jev (TypeSafe) sizes only the effort of each eligible crew:* Agent call, bounded to medium or high; models stay at role defaults or fixed twin ids. Any Jev request or config failure requests medium unless the agent has already sent its first step. The choice shows in the task's description. The call's description and its prompt (secrets and paths removed, cut to 4000 characters) are sent to api.typesafe.ai. Only automatic quota routing may move a call to its role's Codex twin, even without this key, and a base-role call that names a model keeps it. The key is sent only in the Authorization header and is never logged or stored by the plugin. A repository's own settings cannot supply it.
